# Model and source

Zylbersztajn 2021 fitted two independent two-compartment models, one for
vancomycin and one for meropenem, to the same nine children on
extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Each is shipped as its own model
file:

* `Zylbersztajn_2021_vancomycin`:
  `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zylbersztajn_2021_vancomycin"))$description`
* `Zylbersztajn_2021_meropenem`:
  `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zylbersztajn_2021_meropenem"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zylbersztajn_2021_meropenem"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2021.709332> (open access)

# Population

The study was prospective and ran in two paediatric intensive care units in
Santiago, Chile, between July 2017 and November 2019. It enrolled children
under 15 years of age (neonates excluded) who needed ECMO and received
vancomycin and/or meropenem for suspected or confirmed infection. Nine
patients contributed 11 PK profiles per drug: one patient was sampled on three
occasions, two received only vancomycin and two received only meropenem. All
circuits used a polymethylpentene oxygenator with a phosphorylcholine coating.
Five patients were on veno-arterial and four on veno-venous ECMO.

| Characteristic (Tables 1-2) | Vancomycin | Meropenem |
|---|---|---|
| Female / male (n) | 6 / 3 | 5 / 4 |
| Age, months: mean, median (range) | 50.4, 24 (2-132) | 68.3, 48 (2-165) |
| Weight, kg: mean, median (range) | 15.5, 10 (3.5-37) | 20.4, 16 (3.5-45) |
| Serum creatinine, mg/dL: mean, median (range) | 0.34, 0.22 (0.08-1.23) | 0.41, 0.3 (0.08-1.27) |
| CRRT (n) | 2 | 4 |
| Regimen | 10-15 mg/kg as a 2-h infusion q6h or q12h | 20-40 mg/kg as a 3-h infusion q8h or q12h |
| Median daily dose | 54 (20-60) mg/kg/day | 120 (60-120) mg/kg/day |
| Samples | 44 (0.5, 1, 2 h post-infusion and pre-dose) | 33 (1, 3 h post-infusion and pre-dose) |

Unbound concentrations were measured: vancomycin by immunoassay (LLOQ
1.7 mg/L) and meropenem by HPLC-UV (LLOQ 0.16 mg/L). Both models were fitted
with the non-parametric NPAG algorithm in Pmetrics 1.5.0. The same information
is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zylbersztajn_2021_vancomycin")$population`.

# How the parameter values were read

The paper prints each final model as a Pmetrics model file (Tables 3 and 4).
The `#Primary variables` lines of those files are the NPAG **search ranges**,
not estimates. The only numeric results are Tables 5 and 6, which summarise
the individual parameters **per kilogram** (mean, SD, median, CV%, shrinkage).
These tables cannot be a rescaling of the printed primaries. For meropenem,
for example, a V confined to the printed 2-3.5 L range cannot have the 72% CV
that Table 5 reports, and the Table 5 mean of 0.289 L/kg x 20.4 kg = 5.9 L
lies outside that range. The maintainers therefore anchored the **Table 5/6
medians** at each model's reference patient:

* **Central volume** scales linearly with weight in both models
  (`Vw = V*(WGT/ref)`), so a per-kg Vc is exactly the model's own structure:
  Vc = 0.289 L/kg x 20.4 kg (meropenem) and 0.397 L/kg x 15.5 kg (vancomycin).
* **Meropenem clearance** has no weight term (`Ke = CL/Vw`) but is reported per
  kg. It is held flat at its value for the reference weight:
  0.144 L/h/kg x 20.4 kg = 2.94 L/h.
* **Vancomycin clearance** is printed as
  `CLw = CL*(wgt/15.5)*(0.56*(0.34/crea))`. The Table 6 median of
  0.061 L/h/kg is read as CLw per kg at the reference patient (15.5 kg,
  creatinine 0.34 mg/dL), so CLw = 0.9455 L/h there. The literal 0.56
  multiplier is kept as printed, which makes the primary CL
  0.9455 / 0.56 = 1.688 L/h.
* **Kcp and Kpc** are not weight-scaled and are the Table 5/6 medians.

The typical-value checks below pin these anchors.

```{r typical}
mod_v <- readModelDb("Zylbersztajn_2021_vancomycin")
mod_m <- readModelDb("Zylbersztajn_2021_meropenem")

typ_ev <- function(wt, creat) {
  data.frame(
    id = seq_along(wt), time = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
    WT = wt, CREAT = creat
  )
}
wts <- c(3.5, 10, 15.5, 20.4, 45)
typ_v <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_v), typ_ev(wts, 0.34)) |> as.data.frame()
typ_m <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_m), typ_ev(wts, 0.34)) |> as.data.frame()

typ_tab <- data.frame(
  WT = wts,
  vanco_cl_per_kg = typ_v$cl / wts,
  vanco_vc_per_kg = typ_v$vc / wts,
  mero_cl = typ_m$cl,
  mero_vc_per_kg = typ_m$vc / wts
)
typ_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Weight (kg)" = WT,
    "Vancomycin CL (L/h/kg), creatinine 0.34" = vanco_cl_per_kg,
    "Vancomycin Vc (L/kg)" = vanco_vc_per_kg,
    "Meropenem CL (L/h)" = mero_cl,
    "Meropenem Vc (L/kg)" = mero_vc_per_kg
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

stopifnot(
  # Table 6 medians at the vancomycin reference patient.
  abs(typ_v$cl[wts == 15.5] / 15.5 / 0.061 - 1) < 1e-6,
  all(abs(typ_v$vc / wts / 0.397 - 1) < 1e-6),
  # Vancomycin CL per kg is weight-independent at a fixed creatinine.
  all(abs(typ_v$cl / wts / 0.061 - 1) < 1e-6),
  # Table 5 medians for meropenem; CL flat in weight.
  all(abs(typ_m$cl / (0.144 * 20.4) - 1) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(typ_m$vc / wts / 0.289 - 1) < 1e-6)
)
```

Under the literal creatinine term, vancomycin clearance is inversely
proportional to creatinine. Halving creatinine from the reference doubles
clearance:

```{r creat}
typ_c <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_v),
  typ_ev(rep(15.5, 3), c(0.17, 0.34, 0.68))
) |> as.data.frame()
typ_c$cl / typ_c$cl[2]
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_c$cl / typ_c$cl[2] - c(2, 1, 0.5)) < 1e-6))
```

# Source trace

Per-parameter origins are also recorded inline in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Zylbersztajn_2021_vancomycin.R` and
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Zylbersztajn_2021_meropenem.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Vancomycin | Meropenem | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two compartments; first-order elimination and distribution (Kcp, Kpc) | -- | -- | Methods, Model Development; Results |
| `Vw = V*(WGT/ref)` | ref 15.5 kg | ref 20.4 kg | Tables 3, 4 |
| `CLw = CL*(wgt/15.5)*(0.56*(0.34/crea))` | as printed | -- | Table 4 |
| `Ke = CL/Vw` (no covariate on CL) | -- | as printed | Table 3 |
| `Vp = Vc*Kcp/Kpc` (derived, not estimated) | -- | -- | Methods |
| `lcl` | log(0.061 x 15.5 / 0.56) = log(1.688 L/h) | log(0.144 x 20.4) = log(2.94 L/h) | Tables 6, 5: CL median |
| `lvc` | log(0.397 x 15.5) = log(6.15 L) | log(0.289 x 20.4) = log(5.90 L) | Tables 6, 5: Vc median |
| `lk12` (Kcp) | log(0.481 1/h) | log(1.30 1/h) | Tables 6, 5: Kcp median |
| `lk21` (Kpc) | log(0.286 1/h) | log(1.34 1/h) | Tables 6, 5: Kpc median |
| `etalcl` | log(0.922^2 + 1) = 0.6152 | log(0.733^2 + 1) = 0.4300 | Tables 6, 5: CL CV% |
| `etalvc` | log(0.610^2 + 1) = 0.3163 | log(0.720^2 + 1) = 0.4177 | Tables 6, 5: Vc CV% |
| `etalk12` | log(0.630^2 + 1) = 0.3343 | log(0.726^2 + 1) = 0.4234 | Tables 6, 5: Kcp CV% |
| `etalk21` | log(0.458^2 + 1) = 0.1904 | log(0.790^2 + 1) = 0.4850 | Tables 6, 5: Kpc CV% |
| `addSd` | 3 x 2 = 6 mg/L | 1 x 0.2 = 0.2 mg/L | Tables 4, 3: G x C0 |
| `propSd` | 3 x 1 = 3 | 1 x 0.1 = 0.1 | Tables 4, 3: G x C1 |

The Table 5/6 derived rows (Vp, Vd) are means of individual ratios and are not
used by the model. Under the medians, the typical Vp is 0.289 x 1.30 / 1.34 =
0.280 L/kg for meropenem (Table 5 mean 0.317) and 0.397 x 0.481 / 0.286 =
0.668 L/kg for vancomycin (Table 6 mean 0.816; Table 6 prints its unit as
L/h, a misprint for L/kg).

# Two-compartment disposition is real

The models declare `vp` and `q`, so rxode2 integrates the explicit
two-compartment ODEs rather than collapsing `cl` / `vc` to a one-compartment
kernel. The check below solves a single typical infusion at the reference
patient and compares it with the closed-form biexponential infusion solution.
Both sides use the same parameters, so the difference is numerical error only.

```{r biexp}
biexp_infusion <- function(t, dose, dur, cl, vc, k12, k21) {
  k10 <- cl / vc
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  a <- (alpha - k21) / (alpha - beta)
  b <- (k21 - beta) / (alpha - beta)
  r <- dose / dur
  tin <- pmin(t, dur)
  amt <- r * (a / alpha * (exp(-alpha * (t - tin)) - exp(-alpha * t)) +
    b / beta * (exp(-beta * (t - tin)) - exp(-beta * t)))
  amt / vc
}

closed_check <- function(mod, wt, creat, dose, dur) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose, rate = dose / dur, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0.25, 24, by = 0.25), amt = NA, rate = NA, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt, CREAT = creat)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
    as.data.frame()
  ref <- biexp_infusion(s$time, dose, dur, s$cl[1], s$vc[1], s$k12[1], s$k21[1])
  list(sim = s, rel = s$Cc / ref - 1)
}

chk_v <- closed_check(mod_v, 15.5, 0.34, 13.5 * 15.5, 2)
chk_m <- closed_check(mod_m, 20.4, 0.34, 40 * 20.4, 3)
c(vancomycin = max(abs(chk_v$rel)), meropenem = max(abs(chk_m$rel)))
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_v$rel)) < 1e-6, max(abs(chk_m$rel)) < 1e-6)
```

# Virtual cohorts

Each drug gets a cohort of 200 children dosed at the paper's median regimen:

* vancomycin 13.5 mg/kg as a 2-h infusion every 6 h (54 mg/kg/day);
* meropenem 40 mg/kg as a 3-h infusion every 8 h (120 mg/kg/day).

Weight and creatinine are drawn from log-normal distributions with each
cohort's Table 2 median and mean, truncated to the Table 2 range. The
individual covariate values and their correlation are not published, so the
draws are independent. Meropenem does not use creatinine, which is set to the
cohort median. Sampling is at steady state (`ss = 1`), matching the paper's
sampling after 24 h (meropenem) and 48 h (vancomycin) of treatment.

```{r cohorts}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20210813)
n_per_arm <- 200

rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, med, mean, lo, hi) {
  s <- sqrt(2 * log(mean / med))
  u <- stats::runif(n, stats::plnorm(lo, log(med), s), stats::plnorm(hi, log(med), s))
  stats::qlnorm(u, log(med), s)
}

make_events <- function(covs, mg_per_kg, tau, dur) {
  dose <- covs |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = 0, amt = mg_per_kg * WT, rate = amt / dur, ii = tau,
      addl = 24 / tau, ss = 1L, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
    )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = covs$id, time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(covs, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

cov_v <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_per_arm),
  treatment = "Vancomycin 13.5 mg/kg q6h",
  WT = rtrunc_lnorm(n_per_arm, 10, 15.5, 3.5, 37),
  CREAT = rtrunc_lnorm(n_per_arm, 0.22, 0.34, 0.08, 1.23)
)
cov_m <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_per_arm),
  treatment = "Meropenem 40 mg/kg q8h",
  WT = rtrunc_lnorm(n_per_arm, 16, 20.4, 3.5, 45),
  CREAT = 0.3
)
tau_v <- 6
tau_m <- 8
ev_v <- make_events(cov_v, 13.5, tau_v, 2)
ev_m <- make_events(cov_m, 40, tau_m, 3)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_v <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_v, ev_v, maxsteps = 1e6, keep = c("treatment", "WT", "CREAT")) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_m <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_m, ev_m, maxsteps = 1e6, keep = c("treatment", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_v$Cc), !anyNA(sim_m$Cc))
```

```{r vpc-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state unbound concentrations (median and 5th-95th percentiles of the individual predictions) over 24 h at the median regimens. Analogue of Figures 2 (meropenem) and 4 (vancomycin) of Zylbersztajn 2021; the observed data are not published, so no observations are overlaid."}
dplyr::bind_rows(sim_v, sim_m) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = stats::median(Cc),
    lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after a steady-state dose (h)", y = "Unbound concentration (mg/L)")
```

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA summarises the steady-state 24-h window for vancomycin (four doses) and
one 8-h interval for meropenem.

```{r pknca}
nca_run <- function(sim, tau, mg_per_kg, end) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= end) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
  dose <- sim |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, WT) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, end - tau, by = tau)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = mg_per_kg * WT)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = 0, end = end, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE
  )
  # Linear trapezoids: the default log-down rule under-integrates the steep
  # distribution phase of fast-clearing subjects on a 0.25-h grid (up to
  # about 1%), which would blur the AUC identity check below.
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = intervals,
    options = list(auc.method = "linear")
  ))
}
nca_v <- nca_run(sim_v, tau_v, 13.5, 24)
nca_m <- nca_run(sim_m, tau_m, 40, tau_m)
summary(nca_v)
summary(nca_m)
```

At steady state the AUC over 24 h equals the daily dose divided by each
subject's clearance. Both sides use the same drawn parameters, so this checks
the solve and the NCA integration, not the model.

```{r auc-identity}
auc_v <- as.data.frame(nca_v) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_v, id, WT, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rel = PPORRES / (4 * 13.5 * WT / cl) - 1)
auc_m <- as.data.frame(nca_m) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_m, id, WT, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rel = PPORRES / (40 * WT / cl) - 1)
c(vancomycin = max(abs(auc_v$rel)), meropenem = max(abs(auc_m$rel)))
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_v) == n_per_arm, nrow(auc_m) == n_per_arm,
  max(abs(auc_v$rel)) < 5e-3, max(abs(auc_m$rel)) < 5e-3
)
```

# Comparison with the published exposures (Table 7)

Table 7 reports the individual-posterior exposure of each of the 11 PK
profiles. For vancomycin these are the trough and the AUC/MIC at an MIC of
1 mg/L, which equals AUC24 in mg.h/L. For meropenem the table gives the
concentration at half the dosing interval, Cp,t50, which is 1 h after the end
of the 3-h infusion, 4 h after the start of a q8h dose. The medians of the 11
published values are compared with the cohort medians below.
`ncaComparisonTable()` pools by median.

```{r table7}
tab7 <- data.frame(
  trough = c(17.8, 12.7, 18.0, 16.1, 10.7, 13.3, 16.4, 15.3, 23.6, 14.0, 15.9),
  auc_mic = c(558.3, 306.8, 543.0, 492.8, 239.1, 339.6, 547.4, 419.7, 599.2, 394.0, 440.9),
  cp_t50 = c(20.56, 35.00, 64.50, 40.90, 18.70, 101.00, 73.00, 11.20, 28.40, 43.20, 7.30)
)
reference_v <- data.frame(
  treatment = unique(sim_v$treatment),
  auclast = stats::median(tab7$auc_mic),
  cmin = stats::median(tab7$trough)
)
cmp_v <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_v, reference_v,
  by = "treatment", params = c("auclast", "cmin"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmin = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp_v)

cp_t50_sim <- sim_m |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 4)
auc24_sim <- auc_v$PPORRES
target <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Meropenem Cp,t50 median (mg/L)",
    "Meropenem profiles with Cp,t50 > 8 mg/L (%)",
    "Vancomycin profiles with AUC24/MIC > 400 (%)"
  ),
  simulated = c(
    stats::median(cp_t50_sim$Cc),
    100 * mean(cp_t50_sim$Cc > 8),
    100 * mean(auc24_sim > 400)
  ),
  table7 = c(stats::median(tab7$cp_t50), 100 * 10 / 11, 100 * 7 / 11)
)
target |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Simulated" = simulated, "Table 7" = table7) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The deterministic typical patient at the cohort medians isolates the
covariate anchoring from the cohort draw. For vancomycin, weight cancels from
AUC24 because both dose and clearance are per kg, so only creatinine
matters. For meropenem, clearance is flat while the dose is per kg, so weight
matters.

```{r typical-exposure}
typ_v_med <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_v), typ_ev(10, 0.22)) |>
  as.data.frame()
typ_auc_v <- 54 * 10 / typ_v_med$cl
typ_m_ev <- ev_m |>
  dplyr::filter(id == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 16, amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, 40 * 16, NA_real_), rate = amt / 3)
typ_m_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_m), typ_m_ev, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame()
typ_cp_t50 <- typ_m_sim$Cc[typ_m_sim$time == 4]
c(vanco_auc24_typical = typ_auc_v, mero_cp_t50_typical = typ_cp_t50)

stopifnot(
  # Centre of the cohort against the published medians, as a factor. A
  # mis-transcribed clearance, volume, dose or unit (x10, or a per-kg value
  # left unscaled) moves these far outside the band. The cohort also
  # inherits the anchoring offset discussed below, so the band is a factor
  # of 2.5 rather than tight. Realised ratios at 1 / 2 / 4 / 16 threads:
  # AUC24 1.60 / 1.82 / 1.54 / 1.87, Cp,t50 0.82 / 0.78 / 0.73 / 0.80
  # (0.61 in one further render).
  abs(log(stats::median(auc24_sim) / stats::median(tab7$auc_mic))) < log(2.5),
  abs(log(stats::median(cp_t50_sim$Cc) / stats::median(tab7$cp_t50))) < log(2.5),
  # Typical patient, deterministic: 54 mg/kg/day over
  # 0.061 L/h/kg x (0.34 / 0.22) = 572.8 mg.h/L.
  abs(typ_auc_v / (54 * 0.22 / (0.061 * 0.34)) - 1) < 1e-6
)
```

**Meropenem.** The typical patient at the median weight of 16 kg has Cp,t50
`r round(typ_cp_t50, 1)` mg/L, against a published median of 35.0 mg/L. The
cohort median is `r round(stats::median(cp_t50_sim$Cc), 1)` mg/L, and
`r round(100 * mean(cp_t50_sim$Cc > 8))`% of the cohort reach Cp,t50 > 8 mg/L
against 91% in Table 7. Clearance is flat in weight while the dose is per kg,
so the lighter children in the cohort get much less drug per unit clearance
and make up the low tail; the large variability on all four parameters
(CV 72-79%) widens the spread further.
Reading the Table 5 clearance as linear in weight (0.144 L/h/kg x WT) would
raise the light children's exposure, but it contradicts the printed
`Ke = CL/Vw`.

**Vancomycin.** The typical patient at median creatinine has AUC24
`r round(typ_auc_v)` mg.h/L, against a published median of 441 mg.h/L, and
the cohort median is `r round(stats::median(auc24_sim))` mg.h/L. The simulated
trough is high for the same reason. Most of this offset comes from reading the Table 6 per-kg median
as the reference-patient clearance (see the next section); the assumed
creatinine distribution and the large clearance variability (CV 92%) move the
cohort further.

The model parameters were not adjusted to match Table 7.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Final-model primaries unreported.** Tables 3/4 print only the NPAG search
  ranges of the primary variables, and Tables 5/6 provably do not rescale
  them (the CV% exceeds what the ranges allow). The typical values are the
  Table 5/6 per-kg medians anchored at each model's reference patient, as
  described above.
* **Meropenem clearance held flat.** Table 3 has no weight term on clearance,
  so CL = 0.144 L/h/kg x 20.4 kg = 2.94 L/h for every weight. A child far
  from 20.4 kg therefore has a per-kg clearance very different from the
  Table 5 median (0.84 L/h/kg at 3.5 kg, 0.065 L/h/kg at 45 kg). That spread
  is what the printed structure implies; the per-kg reporting suggests the
  individual clearances did not in fact vary this widely with weight.
* **Vancomycin `0.56` term taken literally.** The printed
  `CLw = CL*(wgt/15.5)*(0.56*(0.34/crea))` is encoded as written, with the
  Table 6 median read as CLw at the reference patient. This fixes the
  typical clearance at the reference, and the creatinine effect is linear
  (exponent 1). If the 0.56 were instead an exponent lost in typesetting,
  (0.34/crea)^0.56, the creatinine effect would be weaker and the predicted
  AUC24 at median creatinine would be about 693 rather than 573 mg.h/L.
* **Residual error as printed.** Pmetrics gives SD = G x (C0 + C1 x Y),
  combined linearly (`combined1()`). The vancomycin values (G = 3, C0 = 2,
  C1 = 1) give an additive 6 mg/L plus a 300% proportional error, which is
  implausibly wide for a validated immunoassay; it is shipped as printed. The
  Pmetrics polynomial is in the observed concentration Y, whereas nlmixr2
  evaluates it at the prediction.
* **Non-parametric to parametric.** NPAG estimates a discrete joint density.
  It is represented by independent log-normal random effects whose variances
  reproduce the Table 5/6 CV% (omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)). Correlations are
  not reported.
* **Unbound concentrations.** The paper reports unbound concentrations for
  both drugs. Vancomycin was measured by a standard immunoassay, which
  ordinarily measures total drug; the paper's description is followed.
* **Virtual cohort.** Weight and creatinine are drawn independently from
  truncated log-normal distributions matching the Table 2 median, mean and
  range. All subjects receive the median regimen, whereas the observed
  profiles came from regimens adjusted to renal function (vancomycin 10-15 mg/kg
  q6-12h, meropenem 20-40 mg/kg q8-12h).
* **ECMO and CRRT not covariates.** The ECMO mode (VA/VV) and CRRT (vancomycin
  2, meropenem 4 patients) were not tested or retained; their effect is
  absorbed into the between-subject variability.
* **Table 2 units.** Serum albumin is labelled g/L but its values (median
  3.5-3.55) are g/dL. Albumin was screened and not retained.
